caption:
100M now runs on both Macs with four 25M WebGL tiles. Full-output finite, band, coverage and FP64-reference checks passed. The main figure separates resident placement, placement through host output, and three fresh generation-through-retained-output pipelines. Native FP32 single-core, multicore and Metal baselines are included at 100M; FP64 NumPy remains a distinct precision baseline. Historical 10M native and synthetic raw/Rust detector baselines are retained in separate panels.

These are implementation-and-scope measurements, not a hardware ranking or a precision-neutral speedup claim. WebGL streamed readback differs substantially between the two desktop runs; the cause remains unresolved. Lorium had pre-existing memory pressure and active swap. Raw timing samples, observed ranges, exact output formats, validation cadence and source hashes accompany the figures. No confidence intervals, efficacy claim, angular-order claim or physics claim are inferred.

M5 native outputs passed numerical validation, but a contemporaneous compile log and binary hash tying its executable to the recorded source were not supplied. M4 has the full source-to-binary-to-fixtures-to-output chain.
